subject: Commit amendment: aligning burst usage to steady-state GPUs for EmberAI
messages:
From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Thomas <aisha@emberai.com>, procurement@emberai.com
Cc: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 11 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Commit amendment: aligning burst usage to steady-state GPUs for EmberAI

Aisha — thanks again for walking through May's surge this morning. Per our conversation, EmberAI's burst activity has consistently exceeded the current committed slice during business hours and is driving a material overage. I attached the usage export (CSV) that shows the 7-day rolling 95th percentile for token throughput and sustained GPU hours.

High level ask:
- Can we discuss converting a portion of the burst pool into committed capacity to lower unit cost and remove overage volatility?
- EmberAI indicated readiness to commit but wants a staged approach and a runway for model-mix changes.

Suggested next steps:
1) I can run a sizing proposal based on the attached export (I included a recommended tranche: +12 A100-equivalent GPUs staged over 8 weeks).
2) Rishi and I will align on pricing/term options (6 vs 12 month tranche, canary window).
3) Procurement to confirm approval path and PO timing.

Attachments: emberai-usage-report-may2027.csv (summary rows + hourly spike chart)

Thanks — available 11:30–13:00 PT today for a quick sync if that works.

– Sergio Alvarez
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sergio.alvarez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Aisha Thomas <aisha@emberai.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@emberai.com, devops@emberai.com
Date: Wed, 12 May 2027 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit amendment: aligning burst usage to steady-state GPUs for EmberAI

Sergio — thanks, this is timely. We reviewed the CSV with our infra team. A few notes:

- The surge pattern is real and repeats around our nightly batch re-training and a new high-concurrency inference path launched two weeks ago. Sustained load during peak windows averages ~85% utilization on the current dedicated pool and occasionally spikes to >95% for 20–40 minute windows.
- We are open to committing more capacity but want to avoid being locked into model-specific capacity that becomes stranded if we change model families.

Questions for Redwood:
1) Can you propose a staged conversion that uses burst->commit conversion with a rollback window?
2) What are the expected per-token cost reductions for a 6-month vs 12-month commit for the +12 A100 equivalent tranche?
3) Can you provide an SLA addendum for the committed tranche and a telemetry handoff so our SREs can monitor tail latency after the move?

We can do a 30-minute call Thursday 09:00 PT. Procurement is looped in and will need the proposed amendment and a preliminary pricing table.

Best,
Aisha Thomas
Head of ML Ops, EmberAI
aisha@emberai.com

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, kimberly.park@redwood.com
Cc: aisha@emberai.com
Date: Thu, 13 May 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit amendment: aligning burst usage to steady-state GPUs for EmberAI

Sergio / Kimberly — quick internal run-through after Aisha's notes and the CSV. Key recommendations:

1) Staged commit profile
   - Phase 1 (weeks 0–4): Convert 6 GPUs from burst to committed. Leave 8 GPUs as burst for model experimentation. Apply auto-fallback from committed -> burst for short spikes.
   - Phase 2 (weeks 5–8): Convert additional 6 GPUs if 7-day 95th percentile remains above committed threshold.

2) Canary/rollback
   - 14-day canary on Phase 1 with latency/throughput SLO gates. If tail P99 latency exceeds current baseline by >15% for 3 consecutive days, rollback conversion for affected slot.

3) Pricing/table (ballpark)
   - 6-month commit: ~18% unit discount vs burst list
   - 12-month commit: ~26% unit discount vs burst list
   - We can add a mid-term true-up at month 3 to reconcile usage and avoid stranded capacity charges.

4) Observability handoff
   - Provide per-route token/latency dashboards and token-level cost breakdown for EmberAI; we will create a shared dashboard link.

I attached a draft amendment PDF with the proposed tranche sizes and the SLO gates for the canary. Procurement will need the line-item pricing and DocuSign-ready language.

Thoughts? If Aisha is comfortable with the staged approach we can finalize numbers and generate an amendment for review before the end of week.

– Rishi
Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.com>
To: Aisha Thomas <aisha@emberai.com>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.com>, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@emberai.com
Date: Fri, 15 May 2027 15:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Commit amendment: aligning burst usage to steady-state GPUs for EmberAI

Aisha — appreciate the quick turnaround and clear constraints. EmberAI's ask to avoid model-family lock-in is reasonable; the staged approach gives both runway and optionality.

Confirming next steps from Redwood for procurement: 
- We'll send a formal amendment (DocuSign) that covers Phase 1 (+6 GPUs committed for 6 months) with a 14-day canary and a mid-term true-up at 90 days.
- Attachments: proposed-commit-amendment-EMB-4521.pdf (covers pricing, rollback language, SLO gates) and the usage CSV you provided.
- Pricing: we will include both the 6-month and 12-month options in the amendment; procurement can sign for 6 months now and convert to 12 months in the DocuSign flow if desired.

Please confirm: procurement will need PO details; once received we will provision Phase 1 within 5 business days and kick off the canary with your SREs.

Thanks — looking forward to locking this in.

Kimberly Park
Renewals Lead, Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.com
